scope: Owner-requested proposed five-star implementation of the gold-star reference game, the Day One Mermaid Pool, with the primary coding by Claude and the art and voice generation handed to Codex. Truthful skimmer pickup lines (the leaf line only for the leaf, object-neutral lines otherwise, exact per-object takes preferred when READY); the approved ghost hand points at the next piece, demonstrates the waterfall stroke and taps the seahorse trash; idle re-prompts replay the activity's exact lines twice at most; waterfall progress is the authored dirt wiped from the top, and a touch on another lane retargets the unearned approach; seahorse taps during work queue with full contact per tug and a deliberate pull counts twice; approved soap bubbles and clean rings replace every code-drawn arc, dot, wash and glyph; Roshan keeps her approved colours under the dingy room tint; the probe completes all three activities with real input and adds zero-input, queue, retarget, second-finger and teardown legs. The Pool is re-assessed from 3/5 (17/24) to 4/5 (22/24) on the gold-star scorecard; only device, child and owner acceptance remain. Codex handoff packet GS0-GS4 published with the audit. Packet revision 2 brings the GS2-A action handoff under the owner's 2026-10-03 animation workflow decision merged from dev (DL-MOT-12, DL-MOT-14 to DL-MOT-16): one job card per action, an editable Aseprite master with per-frame hand sockets and lossless export, a clip contract and a scoop pilot. lessons.lesson: Approved guide and effect art already in the repository (ghost hand, soap bubbles, clean ring) replaced every code-drawn shape and glyph in the Pool without generating anything; inventory approved effects before asking for new art.
Completing activities through probe helpers hid dropped taps and wrong-object lines; driving every step with real input exposed them, and mutation tests proved the new checks bite.
A room-wide tint on a shared parent also recolours the character; give her cutouts the exact inverse and fade both together.
